summary: Richard Watson of the Network Information Center proposes a compromise for naming hosts: a formal name made of an institution and a host or station part, plus optional nicknames. He lists the requirements any scheme must meet, as earlier proposals had not been accepted.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo proposes formal host names made from an institution code and a host or station code, with an optional nickname. It asks each site's liaison to choose names and send them to the author by the stated deadline.

subtitle: A proposed host-naming scheme with formal names and optional nicknames.

tldr.problem: Earlier proposals for standard host names, including RFC 247, had not gained acceptance, while sites valued their own names.
tldr.mechanism: The proposal combines an institution mnemonic with a host or NIC-station mnemonic and allows a separate optional nickname.
tldr.outcome: The memo asks site liaisons to submit names by November 5 and obsoletes RFC 237.

today: RFC 273 obsoletes RFC 237. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 273.

sections.title: What a Host-Naming Scheme Must Support
sections.content: The memo says a naming scheme must account for a network that could grow to several hundred sites, the need for abbreviations that are easier to type, the use of names in print and online documents, and people's attachment to historical project names. The author presents a hybrid scheme in response to these needs.
sections.plainLanguage: A naming system should work as the network grows, be easy to type and fit names people already use. This proposal tries to balance those needs.

sections.title: Formal Names and Nicknames
sections.content:
Each host receives a formal name in the form <Institution Mnemonic>-<Host or NIC Station Mnemonic>, plus an optional nickname. The institution mnemonic is at most four characters and can follow the choices described in RFC 247. The host or station mnemonic has no length limit but should be short; suggested choices include a suborganization, project name or machine designation.

The nickname should be unique within the network community and preferably match the host or station mnemonic. The author strongly recommends that Telnet programs recognize both the formal name and nickname.
sections.plainLanguage: The formal name identifies the institution and then the host or station. A separate nickname is optional and should be unique across the network.

sections.title: Choosing Names and Sending Them
sections.content:
Hosts choose their own names through their liaisons. The memo allows discussion if a name is duplicated or very long, and says hosts or stations at one institution should use the same institution mnemonic.

The author asks each liaison to send names by November 5 and asks to hear about implementation difficulties other than those involving TIPs.
sections.plainLanguage: Each site chooses names through its liaison, using one institution code for its hosts. The author asks liaisons to submit their choices by November 5.
